data.text: Zod lets you define schemas that validate unknown data and infer TypeScript types automatically.

data.title: Zod schema

data.text: Parsing Unknown Data at the Boundary

Zod schemas parse `unknown` into a typed value or throw a structured error. The important discipline is to parse at the boundary — the response of a fetch, form input, environment variables — so the rest of the code can trust its types instead of asserting them.

data.title: Parsing an API response

data.text: `safeParse` returns `{ success, data }` or `{ success: false, error }` instead of throwing, which suits form validation. `.transform` changes the parsed value, `.refine` adds a custom check, and `.superRefine` reports several issues at once. Composing smaller schemas with `.extend` and `.merge` keeps them reusable.

data.title: Form validation with safeParse
Interview angle: validate at the edge, trust inside
data.text: The reason Zod matters is not the syntax but where the parse happens. Validation at the boundary turns the entire codebase into typed, trustworthy code with no runtime surprises; sprinkling checks in random places does the opposite by giving a false sense of safety. Say that you parse once at the edge and let the type system carry the guarantee inward.
